metadata.title: Hydraulic Cylinder Force
metadata.topic: Cylinder force from pressure and piston area

learningPurpose: Prepare the hydraulic cylinder force simulation to cite its equation, assumptions, input ranges and safety boundaries.

definitions.meaning: The ideal training-case force calculated from cylinder pressure and piston area before real-world losses or equipment limits are considered.

governingPrinciples: Use pressure in pascals and piston area in square metres.
The ideal training equation does not establish a real cylinder rating.
Fault-mode reductions used in the simulation are pedagogical until reviewed source evidence is onboarded.
assumptions: Pressure is uniform over the piston area.
Piston area is the effective area used for the training case.
The calculation ignores friction, leakage, acceleration, and mechanical limits.
limitations: Does not provide cylinder selection, pressure rating, burst pressure, seal specification, or maintenance guidance.
Simulation input ranges are training constraints, not manufacturer limits.

workedExample.title: Ideal cylinder force
workedExample.purpose: Show traceability for the simulation calculation.

normalOperation: Normal simulation operation calculates ideal force from validated SI inputs.
commonMisconceptions: Assuming an ideal calculated force is a certified lifting capacity.
Using gauge behaviour or leak percentages as manufacturer data.
Treating simulation pressure limits as equipment ratings.

faultConditions.title: Pressure loss
symptoms: Displayed force is lower than the ideal pressure-area result.
likelyCauses: Possible loss mechanism in a real system requiring qualified inspection
faultConditions.safeResponse: Use the condition only inside the reviewed simulation until real diagnostic source evidence is available.

safety.warning: Hydraulic systems can store hazardous energy; a training simulation is not operational authorisation.
safety.studentBoundary: Students must not inspect, adjust, disconnect, or operate hydraulic equipment unless supervised under approved procedures.
